Auger Hollingsworth Accident & Injury Lawyers is an Ontario personal injury law firm serving clients in Ottawa, the Greater Toronto Area and communities across the province. Founded in Ottawa in 2004, the firm has expanded its presence to include offices in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton, Barrie and Hamilton. The firm represents people and families affected by serious accidents, injuries and denied disability claims.

Richard Auger founded the firm after beginning his legal career in criminal defence. He started with one client file and worked from shared office space with another law firm. Several months later, his wife, Brenda Hollingsworth, joined the practice as an equal partner. Brenda brought extensive experience in litigation and personal injury law.

The firm grew through the founders’ commitment to their clients, strong legal advocacy and word-of-mouth referrals. Early recognition included a bronze award in the Ottawa Business Journal’s New Business of the Year category in 2006.

Since then, Auger Hollingsworth has continued to expand while maintaining the personal approach that shaped the firm in its earliest years.

Personal Injury Representation Across Ontario

Today, Auger Hollingsworth Accident & Injury Lawyers focuses on helping injured people and their families navigate personal injury and disability insurance claims.

The firm assists clients with matters involving:

Car accidents and other motor vehicle collisions

Slip and fall accidents

Long-term disability claim denials

Wrongful death claims

Bicycle and pedestrian accidents

Motorcycle accidents

Commercial truck accidents

Other serious injury claims

The firm serves clients throughout Ontario. Consultations may be available by phone, video conference or in person, depending on the client’s circumstances and location.

Clients work with a legal team that includes lawyers, law clerks and experienced support professionals. Each matter receives legal oversight, clear communication and attention based on the client’s needs.

Meet the Founders

Auger Hollingsworth Professional Corporation was founded by Richard Auger and Brenda Hollingsworth. They are law partners and husband and wife.

Richard and Brenda have built their practices around advocacy, client service and legal education. Their work has included representing injured people, families and individuals facing difficult legal disputes.

Both founders have written legal resources for the public and contributed articles to legal publications. They have also been invited to comment on legal issues in the media and share their knowledge through teaching and professional education.

Their experience, combined with the work of the firm’s broader legal team, supports Auger Hollingsworth’s ability to serve clients across Ontario.

Professional Recognition

Richard Auger, Brenda Hollingsworth and the firm have received recognition for their legal work, professional contributions and community involvement.

The firm’s growth from a small Ottawa practice into an Ontario personal injury law firm reflects its continued commitment to advocacy and client service.

Professional awards and distinctions can help demonstrate a lawyer’s standing within the legal and business communities. However, every case is different, and past results do not guarantee a particular outcome.

Commitment to Clients

Personal injury and disability claims can involve complex legal, medical and insurance issues. Clients may be dealing with pain, financial pressure, uncertainty and major changes to their daily lives.

Auger Hollingsworth aims to provide clear and compassionate legal guidance throughout the claims process. The legal team can investigate the circumstances of an accident, collect evidence, communicate with insurers, assess damages and pursue compensation when appropriate.

The firm’s approach is based on careful preparation, direct communication and an understanding of the challenges injured people and their families may face.

Community Involvement and Pro Bono Work

Community service has been an important part of Auger Hollingsworth since the firm opened in 2004. Its involvement has focused on charitable giving, pro bono legal work and public legal education.

In one significant pro bono matter, the firm represented approximately 150 families whose relatives with developmental disabilities were living at the Rideau Regional Centre. After the Ontario government announced plans to close the centre, Brenda Hollingsworth sought an injunction so families could be heard before placement decisions were finalized.

The legal process gave residents and their families an opportunity to participate in decisions about where their loved ones would live in the community. The firm later continued to provide free legal guidance to some affected families.

Richard Auger and Brenda Hollingsworth have also volunteered with the Child Advocacy Project. The program assists children from low-income families who require legal support for education-related matters. Their work included helping children with learning disabilities or autism and their families address concerns involving accommodation and discrimination in the public education system.

Richard also served on the Legal Pursuit Team for the Ottawa Hospital Foundation’s Legacy Campaign. The campaign raised funds for hospital facilities, equipment, research and education.

Charitable Support

Auger Hollingsworth has supported charitable and community initiatives connected to health, education, access to justice and injury prevention.

Organizations and initiatives supported by the firm have included:

The Ottawa Hospital

The Multiple Sclerosis Society

The Canadian Cancer Society

The United Way

The Ottawa Food Bank

Christie Lake Kids

Helmets on Kids

Organizations supporting people affected by spinal cord and brain injuries

The firm has also participated in fundraising activities within the legal community.

Contributions to Legal Education

Richard Auger and Brenda Hollingsworth have both contributed to legal education and professional development.

Richard has lectured in criminal trial advocacy at the University of Ottawa Faculty of Law. He also served as a volunteer coach and mentor for the university’s Arnup Cup advocacy team. Under his mentorship, the team won the Arnup Cup in 2006 and placed third in the national Sopinka Cup competition.

Brenda has taught trial advocacy at the University of Ottawa Faculty of Law. She has also spoken to law students and young lawyers at programs organized by the Ontario Bar Association and has taught advanced civil litigation to prospective law clerks at Algonquin College.

These contributions reflect the founders’ commitment to strengthening the legal profession and helping students and emerging legal professionals develop practical advocacy skills.

An Ontario Personal Injury Law Firm

Auger Hollingsworth began as a small Ottawa law practice and has grown into a personal injury firm serving clients throughout Ontario. Its history remains closely connected to Ottawa, while its legal services now extend across the Greater Toronto Area and other Ontario communities.

The firm continues to be guided by the principles that shaped its early growth: strong advocacy, personal attention, clear communication and a commitment to helping injured people and their families.

At Barriston Law, we provide thoughtful legal services and practical guidance with a client-focused approach rooted in trust, accessibility, and strong community connections. We work closely with individuals, families, businesses, and organizations across Central Ontario, offering support that is responsive, approachable, and grounded in real-world experience.

Our lawyers and staff bring together a wide range of legal knowledge and decades of experience serving clients throughout the region. As one of the largest law firms in Central Ontario, we continue to grow alongside the communities we serve, adapting to changing client needs while maintaining the personal attention people expect from a local firm.

As a proud B Corp Certified firm and recognized Living Wage employer, we are committed to supporting our people and contributing to the communities where we live and work. Community involvement, mentorship, and long-term relationship building are important parts of our culture and help us continue providing consistent service for our clients over time.

As the legal landscape evolves, Barriston Law continues to invest in innovation, accessibility, and client service. Whether you are resolving a dispute, planning for the future, or navigating an important life or business decision, our team is committed to providing clear communication, practical advice, and dependable legal support tailored to your circumstances.

Bartlet & Richardes LLP is a Windsor, Ontario law firm with senior litigation lawyer, Mary-Joe Renaud recognized by Best Lawyers across two practice areas, including Insurance Law and Personal Injury Litigation. The firm provides legal services to individuals, families, and organizations across the province. The firm’s practice includes insurance law, personal injury litigation, corporate, real estate, commercial litigation, employment law, family law, and a broad range of civil matters. Its lawyers focus on understanding each client’s circumstances and explaining legal options in a clear, practical manner so clients can make informed decisions.

The firm has received peer recognition through Best Lawyers, with one of its lawyers first acknowledged in 2010. This recognition is based on confidential peer review and reflects the views of other lawyers practicing in the same geographic area and fields of law. Bartlet & Richardes LLP has also been included in Best Law Firms listings for personal injury litigation and insurance law, reflecting its ongoing work in these areas.

Bartlet & Richardes LLP represents clients in insurance disputes, accident claims, and related litigation. The firm’s lawyers regularly work with insurers, opposing counsel, and the courts, managing matters from initial assessment through resolution. Their approach emphasizes preparation, timely communication, and responsiveness throughout the life of a case.

Established in 1887, Bartlet & Richardes LLP is one of Windsor’s long-standing law firms. While the firm has undergone name changes over the years, it has remained closely connected to the Windsor community since its early days. The Bartlet family, who settled in Windsor in the mid-19th century, played an active role in local business and civic life, contributing to institutions and landmarks that remain part of the city’s history.

Although there are no longer Bartlet family members with the firm, its foundation has continued for well over a century. Now operating as Bartlet & Richardes LLP, the firm has advised a wide range of clients, including work related to the incorporation of Ford of Canada, representation of Hiram Walker, and matters involving St. Clair College. Over time, lawyers from the firm have also gone on to serve as judges of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, with some appointed to the Ontario Court of Appeal.

The firm practices in most areas of law, with the exception of criminal law. For further information, please review the section Areas of Practice.

The team at Bartlet & Richardes LLP includes partners and associates committed to serving clients with professionalism and care. Additional information is available on the Partners & Associates page.
